newsitem.title: UK: Wait for FOMC saps will to trade Bradys.
newsitem.headline: Wait for FOMC saps will to trade Bradys.

text.p: There was very little trading in emerging debt on Monday, with few investors prepared to take the plunge until the meeting of U.S. monetary policy decision-makers tomorrow.
"There's not a lot going on. If anything the market opened a touch stronger," one broker said.
He pointed to slight rises in Brazil C bonds BR8014=RR and Russian dollar Vneshekonombank paper RUVNUSLNS=RR.
But traders said the market is almost static ahead of Tuesday's FOMC meeting.
In a Reuters poll last week, 34 out of 48 economists said they expected the Fed to raise the federal funds rate at least 25 bps to 5.50 percent at the meeting.
"The key is whether it is a one-off rise or the start of a cycle of increases," said one U.S. bank trader.
A number of traders said a quarter point increase is already priced in but the reaction of Bradys if a rise is announced will remain initially in the hands of U.S. Treasuries.
During the wait, news out of individual countries, much of it fairly positive recently, is having almost no impact.
One of the more positive events has been the deal between the International Monetary Fund and Bulgaria on a new standby programme.
"(It) will unleash sequences of good news in April and the months that follow until the introduction of a currency board in July," ING Barings said.
However, the upside for Bulgarian Bradys is likely to be capped by overall market weakenss and relativce credit weakness, it added.
The bank set three-month targets for spreads over U.S. Treasuries for Bulgarian discount bonds of 990 basis points, 800 for FLIRBs and 780 for IABs.
